subject: Dedicated pilot economics & GPU slate — post-call anchors and next steps
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finpilot.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-15T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated pilot economics & GPU slate — post-call anchors and next steps

Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the anchors we agreed would help us put together a pilot quote and SOW: 

1) Expected token volumes
- Baseline (steady-state): ~15M tokens / month
- Peak window: ~60M tokens / month (burst traffic during end-of-quarter flows)
- Average request size: ~450 tokens

2) Target unit economics
- You indicated comfort with a target in the range of $600–$900 per 1M tokens for a reserved/dedicated offering (pilot pricing + commit). Please confirm your preferred anchor within that range.

3) Throughput & latency targets
- Latency SLO: p95 < 250ms for 1-2 request tokens steady-state; p95 < 350ms during peak bursts
- Throughput anchor: sustained 120–150 tokens/sec across the service; burst capacity to 400 tokens/sec for short spikes

4) Hardware preference (prelim)
- Our recommendation for latency-sensitive UIs is H100-based reserved lanes (2x H100 gives the headroom you described).
- Cost-sensitive option: A100 80GB lanes (cheaper per-hour, slightly higher latency for long-context runs).

Next steps from our side: Ben will drop a short cost worksheet showing the per-1M token economics across 2xH100, 4xA100, and a hybrid fallback configuration, and we’ll attach an initial pilot SOW with a 30-day trial window. From your side: confirmation of the target $/1M anchor and procurement contact (cc'd) so we can route pricing.

Attachments: FP-pilot-econ.xlsx (worksheet), gpu-slate-comparison.pdf (quick hardware tradeoffs)

Thanks — I’ll draft the SOW as soon as we have your cost anchor.

—Grace O'Connor
Principal Sales, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finpilot.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@finpilot.com>
Date: 2027-09-15T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pilot economics & GPU slate — post-call anchors and next steps

Thanks Grace — good summary. Quick answers: 

- Anchor: can you price the pilot at $700 / 1M tokens as the preliminary anchor (we may push for $650 in procurement).
- We can commit to the baseline 15M tokens/mo for the pilot; if the pilot is successful we are likely to commit to a 6–12 month reserved lane.
- Procurement contact is Stephanie Patel — procurement@finpilot.com (cc'd). She will need a one-page quotation and a short SOW to start internal approval.

Can you also include an explicit fallback plan if by month-end we spike beyond the reserved capacity (burst pricing or auto-fallback to a lower-cost model)? Procurement will expect clarity there.

Alex
CTO, FinPilot

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finpilot.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-16T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pilot economics & GPU slate — post-call anchors and next steps

Alex — looping in the cost worksheet and a short note on the unit economics. See attached FP-pilot-econ.xlsx and gpu-slate-comparison.pdf. Key points pulled from the sheet: 

1) Pricing anchors (pilot, per 1M tokens) — these are illustrative, exact numbers subject to final commit length and support tier:
- 2x H100 reserved lane: $680 / 1M tokens (assumes 60% utilization across pilot month; includes autoscaling buffer + prefix caching uplift)
- 4x A100 80GB lanes (cost-optimized): $740 / 1M tokens (higher ops overhead for longer tail latency)
- Hybrid (2x H100 primary + 2x A100 spill): $710 / 1M tokens (best balance of latency & unit cost)

2) Throughput mapping (sustained / burst)
- 2x H100: sustained ~140 tokens/sec, burst ~420 tokens/sec for short windows (30–120s)
- 4x A100: sustained ~110 tokens/sec, burst ~320 tokens/sec

3) Burst/fallback plan
- If you exceed reserved capacity we can provision short-term burst capacity at an incremental rate (line-item in the SOW) or route excess traffic to a compatible lower-cost variant (quantized LLM) with an automatic fall-over policy. Both options are documented in the attached comparison.

4) Risk & limits
- Large-context jobs (>4k tokens) will consume proportionally more GPU mem and may require the H100 option; the worksheet flags that for your 3% large-context traffic.

Next steps we propose:
- Grace: send the 1-page pilot quote and SOW draft with the $700 anchor (as Alex requested).
- Alex / Procurement: indicate whether procurement prefers a short pilot PO or a 30-day contract with auto-convert clause.
- Schedule a 45-min technical deep-dive next week (Ben + infra team) to validate throughput numbers with a sample trace.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Alex / Stephanie — copying Marissa to flag commercial for any discount guardrails. We’ll move forward with the $700 / 1M anchor for the pilot quote and include both burst-pricing and bandwidth-fallback language.

Concrete deliverables today: 
- Ben: updated worksheet with final rows for a 30-day pilot PO and an alternate 30-day trial with an auto-convert to a 6-month reserved commitment.
- Marissa: will prepare a commercial note with max discount of 12% and approvals path.
- Grace: I’ll draft the one-page quote + short SOW and share a DocuSign link.

Proposed calendar: Technical deep-dive (Ben + infra) — Tue Sep 21 10:00–10:45 PT. Does that work for your infra team?

Cheers — will send the SOW in the next 24 hours.
